title: SSK decrease
sourceNotes: SSK is a standard technique described in Weldon's Practical Knitter (1880s series, public domain). The knitwise-slip method is the modern industry-standard form per Craft Yarn Council. sourceType: SYNTHESISED.

glossaryTerms.definition: Slip, slip, knit: two stitches slipped individually knitwise, then knitted together through their front loops. Produces a left-leaning decrease.

content.text: The secret of the
ssk

(slip, slip, knit) is that slipping each stitch knitwise re-orients it on the needle. When the two slipped stitches are knitted together, the decrease leans to the left and its leading leg shows cleanly on the fabric surface. This mirrors a
k2tog
, which leans to the right. The two form a symmetrical pair used in all lace and raglan shaping.
You need yarn and needles. Practise on a swatch of at least 20 stitches in a smooth yarn so the lean of the decrease column is visible.
Step by step
Slip the first stitch from the left needle to the right needle as if to knit. Insert the right needle from left to right into the front of the stitch and slide it across without working it.
Slip the second stitch from the left needle to the right needle in the same way, as if to knit.
Insert the left needle into the front legs of both slipped stitches, from left to right.
Knit both stitches together through their front legs in the normal way. Two stitches have been reduced to one, and the resulting stitch leans to the left.
Where you'll see it

SSK is paired with k2tog in lace patterns, where the lean of each decrease guides the eye along the motif. It also appears in raglan sleeve shaping (left-leaning decreases on the right edge of the seam) and in the gusset decreases after a sock
heel turn
. Most symmetrical shaping in knitting relies on ssk and k2tog as a mirrored pair.
Common faults

Slipping as if to purl instead of as if to knit. Slipping purlwise does not re-orient the stitch, so the resulting decrease will be twisted rather than leaning cleanly to the left. The slip motion for ssk is always knitwise: right needle tip enters from left to right.

Decrease leaning to the right. If the finished decrease column leans right rather than left, the two slipped stitches were knitted together through the back legs rather than the front. After transferring both slipped stitches back to the left needle with the left needle, the right needle must enter from left to right through the front legs.
Loose stitch at the decrease. SSK can be slightly looser than k2tog because the re-orientation requires two separate slipping motions. Snug the working yarn gently after completing the stitch.
What to try next: practise ssk and
k2tog
on the same swatch side by side and compare the lean of the two columns before using them in a pattern.
